html:
Ashgabat is the capital of Turkmenistan, between the Karakum Desert and the Kopet Dag mountains, close to the Iranian border. Russia founded it in 1881 as a fort beside a village of the Teke Turkmen, after crushing Turkmen resistance at Geok Tepe nearby.

It grew as a station on the Trans-Caspian Railway and the main town of Russia's Transcaspian region. In 1924 it became the capital of the Turkmen Soviet republic, under the name Poltoratsk until 1927. On 6 October 1948 the Ashgabat earthquake flattened it and killed tens of thousands of people, news the Soviet government kept quiet.

After independence in 1991, President Saparmurat Niyazov, who called himself Turkmenbashi, "head of the Turkmen", rebuilt the centre as a "white city" of marble-clad palaces and monuments, including a golden statue of himself that turned to face the sun. In 2013 it entered the Guinness World Records as the city with the most white marble buildings. Just outside lie the ruins of Nisa, an early capital of the Parthian Empire.
